extractions.value: Clinical features: progressive difficulty bending left knee, tightness of musculature, spontaneous twitching and visible spasms of left quadriceps, increasing stiffness in lower extremities and lower trunk, sudden jerks evoked by touch or surprise leading to falls. EMG: spontaneous near continuous motor unit activity in left quadriceps, disappearing with voluntary activation. Antibody: serum anti-GAD65 antibodies very high (>25,000 units/mL). Response to treatment: diazepam and baclofen mildly reduced frequency of spasms and severity of stiffness.

extractions.value: Patient had a significant drug reaction to third rituximab exposure (progressive rashes on face/trunk, fever, nausea). Declined prednisone due to concern over weight gain. Did not tolerate reduced dexamethasone dose of 12 mg x 3 days every 2 weeks due to migraines. IVIG discontinuation led to symptom recurrence after 5.5 weeks, with rapid resolution upon resumption. Residual catch at knees persists.
